correctness.rationale: The field-product quotient forces every involution residue to be a sign vector and detects invertibility of a−v coordinate by coordinate. For a fixed sign vector let D be its diagonal involution and set p=(1+v)/2 and p₀=(1+D)/2. The element g=pp₀+(1−p)(1−p₀) is 1 modulo the nilpotent radical and intertwines p₀ and p, proving transitivity of 1+J on the lifts. Its stabilizer has precisely the same-sign Peirce coordinates free, so the orbit has q to the symmetrized cut weight elements, with dimensions over the base field even for nonsplit quotient fields. Summing only admissible sign orbits yields the fibre law, and a sign can always be chosen at each coordinate. In characteristic two the element 1 has no such decomposition because all involutions reduce to 1. Taking the negative of a sign involution as the probe makes just that sign admissible; the singleton plus singleton minus pair cut identity extracts twice the pair weight. The extremal conditions follow from positive summands; any free coordinate yields at least two summands. The two radical-square-zero oriented paths in the record have the same symmetrized weights and equal-sized residue classes, but their directed source and sink types differ even after reversal. The exact T₂ case checks the recovery formula (q·q/1=q²); the supplied finite enumerator was inspected but not executed.
residual_risks: The five recorded small-algebra tests do not enumerate nonsplit field products or directly certify inverse reconstruction; those statements follow from the proof.

originality.rationale: Fixed-diagonal involution counts for incidence algebras and existence of unit-plus-involution decompositions by formal matrix inheritance are antecedents. The supported distinct claim is the exact count for every target element over an arbitrary field-product semisimple quotient, together with recovery of all labelled symmetrized radical dimensions from forced-sign counts and its orientation obstruction. The strongest inspected exact counts either use a matrix simple quotient, specialize to incidence algebras or count all involutions without the target-dependent unit condition. None of these gives the whole recovery theorem on the stated domain. This is a best-of-knowledge comparison, not a claim that orbit counting or the weighted cut identity is new.
residual_risks: The precise content of the untranslated 2019 proceedings predecessor was not verified. An earlier equivalent masked cut-count reconstruction or an unindexed idempotent-lifting application remains possible; the focused external search added no relevant evidence.

value.rationale: This upgrades an existence question to an exact distribution over targets and shows that an additive decomposition count is a probe for an otherwise hidden, labelled radical invariant. It specifies which off-diagonal information survives, with a nonisomorphism and non-anti-isomorphism witness for the information lost. The result is useful beyond triangular or square-zero examples and is not just a count for one algebra or a restatement of existence.
residual_risks: The inverse uses the labelled quotient probes and known q; it does not reconstruct directions, multiplication, diagonal radical dimensions, or the graph from an unlabelled histogram.
